title: Introduction
description: Lupis Engine is an open-source 2D game engine and visual studio for building platformers, top-down RPGs, and visual novels.

blocks.content: **Lupis Engine** combines a visual scene editor, a modular component system, and node-based visual scripting in a single workspace. You can design levels, wire gameplay logic without writing code, and test your game with one click.

blocks.content: Every game in Lupis Engine is built from four core building blocks that work together in real time.

items.title: Scenes & Layers
items.desc: Organize levels into camera-tracked world layers and screen-fixed user interface (UI) layers.

items.title: Entities & Components
items.desc: Build characters, props, and tilemaps by attaching modular visual, physics, and audio components.

items.title: Visual Scripting
items.desc: Create gameplay mechanics by connecting event, action, and helper nodes on an interactive graph.

items.title: Instant Preview & Export
items.desc: Playtest changes immediately in the viewport and package finished games for web or desktop.

rows: Groups entities into ordered rendering planes for gameplay worlds and heads-up display (HUD) overlays.
Represents any object in your game; a **prefab** saves a configured entity as a reusable template.
Adds specific capabilities to an entity, such as [Visual Renderers](components/renderers), [Physics Body](components/physics_body), or [Multi-Collider](components/multi_collider).
Defines how entities react to input, collisions, timers, and game state using connected nodes.

blocks.content: You build a game by assembling entities in a scene, attaching components for appearance and physics, and wiring node graphs for behavior.

items: Open Lupis Engine in your browser or launch the desktop app (see [Installation & Setup](getting_started/installation)).
Create a project on the **My Projects** dashboard to open the [Editor Overview](interface/editor_overview) workspace.
Add entities in the **Scene Hierarchy** and arrange them in the [Scene Viewport](interface/scene_viewport).
Select an entity and click **Add Component** in the **Property Inspector** to attach sprites, colliders, or animations.
Attach a [Script Controller](components/script_controller) and connect nodes from the [Node Library](node_library/overview) to control movement, combat, or UI.
Click **Play** in the top bar to test your game live, then package it in [Project & Export](getting_started/project_and_export).

blocks.content: Lupis Engine includes high-level gameplay nodes tailored for common 2D genres so you can prototype complete mechanics in minutes.

rows: Gravity, variable jumping, wall sliding, sloped terrain, and melee combos.
8-way normalized movement, directional animations, tilemaps, and area triggers.
Typewriter dialogue, branching choice menus, audio sliders, and data-bound HUDs.
